findings.evidence: DCS/event-log/surveillance reconstruction p.60 (clocks mismatched, shifted to real time; explosion 11:22 p.m. p.60): ACSR metal sensors stopped 11:20-11:21 p.m., ACSR A+B dP fell to nearly zero starting 11:21-11:22 p.m., near-ACSR sensors stopped/spiked after 11:23 p.m., fire intensified over ~35 min p.21; Fig.44 spikes 11:30 p.m./11:23 p.m./11:57 p.m. with fire-intensity changes p.62. Post-incident ACSR: 3 major breaches - partial loss north cap sheet + portions of several layers + 2 holes in B-inlet header p.21 (field ruled piping/header-connection breach not initial p.21); 12 different breaches in A-Train equipment/piping/vessels analyzed, ACSR most likely initial p.62. Lab: clear service thermal fatigue at several locations p.22; Table 1 p.22 eliminates over-pressurization (A <1,050 psig vs 1,200 MAWP, B <480 vs 570 p.22), water/ice (moisture analyzers alarmed none in 24 hr p.22), corrosion (Sept 2015 header removal none noted p.22), mercury (B-Train tests only trace, ACSR none p.22), thermal shock (night-of ~3F/min peaking 6F/min p.22). Truss: fin-to-cap/parting braze holds pressurized layers p.15; pushing/pulling fatigues metal to cracks leaking to atmosphere or blocked pass p.16. History: 9 HETSCO repairs on 4 BAHXs with external-only exam p.66; ACSR Table 8 LOCs/cracks p.67. Screening runs (propane surrogate - ASSUMPTION with reason: NGL composition withheld, propane illustrates cryogenic liquid behavior; Fahrenheit service preserved): fluid_properties at 34.11 bar: -67.8C (-90F p.59) density 615.1 kg/m3 vapour 0.0, -45.6C (-50F cryogenic threshold per p.12 n.7) density 590.77 kg/m3 vapour 0.0; bubble_pressure 0.28 bar at -67.8C, 0.87 bar at -45.6C; run_process CORR-PROP-HEAT: NGL-FEED 1.63 m3/h vapour 0.0 to NGL-WARM 1.69 m3/h vapour 0.0, heater duty 12.6 kW.
findings.limiting_value: ACSR MAWP 1,200 psig A-pass, 570 psig B-pass p.22 (not exceeded night-of p.22); BAHX ROC Table 3 p.32: 3.6F/min start-up/shutdown, 1.8F/min normal p.36, 108F in hour p.32; MOC metal ROC alert 1.9F/min, safe upper 3.6F/min, incident setpoint 14.25F/min without MOC p.41
findings.modification: Remove/replace fatigue-cracked ACSR core; do not return BAHX with sealed blocked passes and repeated external weld repairs to cycling two-phase service
findings.unit: ACSR A-Train cold side reboiler BAHX core - initial failure point

findings.evidence: No-shock night reconciled: Table 1 p.22 Thermal shock No - night-of DCS ~3F/min peaking 6F/min p.22, average below 3.6F/min shutdown limit p.32. Sudden rupture = accumulated fatigue reaching critical size with curtailment as final load, not proven night-of exceedance. Curtailment context: Tri-States downstream problems, board operator reduced Tri-States flow, bullets limited so NGL production reduced p.18; non-routine activity, experienced board operator, from control room p.13; 2 personnel, no abnormal alarms/indicators before 11:22 p.m. explosion p.13; within minute second alarm p.13; throughput at incident ~500 MMscf/d raw gas and 16,000-18,000 bpd NGL vs design 1.5 Bcf/d and 50,000 bpd p.58 (~33% gas, 32-36% NGL - part-load history). Mechanism for accumulation: midstream upsets requiring reduce/stop production causing upsets p.33; turndown/start-up/shutdown changes boiling regime, B-pass unstable, liquid-vapor oscillation, rapid localized T fluctuation p.34; single large delta-T shock also described p.16 but excluded night-of by p.22. Dose history: Fig.28 bins 1.8-3.6, 3.6-12.6, 12.6-21.6, 21.6-30.6, >30.6F/min p.37 with routine exceedances; Fig.29 metal ROC ~4-10x damped vs stream p.38 (metal exceedance 2-3% of time in 2011 p.38); guidance gap - no basis comparing 100C/min vs 5C/min, no model-vs-history p.36. Blocked-in screening (same surrogate ASSUMPTION): blocked_in_pressure from 34.11 bar -67.8C to -45.6C returns 303.0 bar (4,380 psig) at 12.1 bar/K, beta 0.00186/K, kappa 0.000153/bar, critical fill 0.955, vapour-pressure regime 0.9 bar if <96% liquid - illustrates trapped-liquid pressurization hazard qualitatively only, not night-of pressure.
findings.limiting_value: Night-of ~3F/min avg, 6F/min peak p.22 vs 3.6F/min shutdown / 1.8F/min normal p.32/p.36; let-burn vent to flare/atmosphere philosophy p.19 available for controlled depressuring

findings.evidence: BP operated almost entire life to June 2016, transition to Enterprise changed corporate support not onsite personnel/procedures p.40. 2012 replacement evaluated, vendors given cycling exemplar data p.42; Chart: dummy-layer exchangers no less susceptible to thermal stress, blocked layer if pressurized can fail catastrophically if not vented p.42; Linde dummy layers purposely blocked with vent holes to atmosphere p.41 n.100/p.42. BP GP-26-10 recommends BAHX for cryogenic (A-Train service) but advises against BAHX in fluctuating-temp or two-phase service - reboilers had both p.41; BP superseded replace recommendation with metal sensors p.41. Sensors/alarms: Fig.30 side-bar locations p.41; procedure to <3.5F/min core p.41; added metal ROC alarms p.41; 2010 leak review of 30 days inlet/outlet (not metal) temps, flow-change deviations worst on quick shutdown/startup, high quantity lower-magnitude excursions also causal p.41 n.97, no action items p.41; 2011 leak no incident report p.41. Repairs/MOC: 14 MOC entities guidance p.44; HETSCO asked if blocking passes reduces stress and if Chart approves - yes to both, leak perceived as contamination only p.44; PGP sealed vent holes contrary to standards, only PGP sealed vs silicone-vented elsewhere p.45; silicone efficacy/size/pressure not calculated p.45 n.117; 2015 vent status no record - ASSUMPTION with reason: PGP sealed practice p.45 cited as basis, weak - requires verification. LBB misuse: requires low growth + non-dangerous fluid + in-service monitoring + calc < critical p.46, none met for cryogenic flammable auto-ignition/explosion release. RAGAGEP: Table 2 four associations p.43; API only ANSI p.31; compliance by any one p.31; most guidance not mechanical-integrity inspection/maintenance focused p.43.
findings.limiting_value: MOC/PSM: alarm desensitized ~7x (14.25 vs 1.9/3.6F/min p.41) without MOC justification p.41; RAGAGEP Table 2 p.43 / Table 3 p.32 limits with gaps p.31/p.36; firm capacity per rules (largest unit out) - ASSUMPTION with reason: no station firm-capacity table in available pages, plant totals p.58 only, so firm-capacity ranking not determinable, noted as gap
findings.modification: PSM/mechanical-integrity overhaul: PHA revalidation for BAHX thermal fatigue, MOC for every repair/alarm change, restore 1.9/3.6F/min alarms p.41, prohibit sealed blocked passes without manufacturer approval with vented/open + leak test + replacement rule after repeat LOCs, fatigue-dose tracking, industry RAGAGEP revision (API 662/ALPEMA/Chart/GPA Table 2 p.43 Table 3 p.32)
